title: Check yourself: what a method reference costs and how overloads resolve

questions.stem: Per this page, what separates a method reference from its equivalent lambda in the bytecode and in speed?

options.text: An extra object per call for the lambda, which makes the reference faster
options.says: The page says both use an invokedynamic call site and perform effectively the same.

options.text: A reflective lookup per call for the reference, which makes the lambda faster
options.says: The page names no reflection: both compile to invokedynamic, and their runtime performance is effectively the same.

options.text: A private synthetic method for the lambda body, with no change in performance
options.says: The page says only the lambda's body becomes a synthetic lambda method, and that the two run equally fast, so readability decides.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

questions.stem: Per this page, what does the compiler do with ambiguousMethod(System.out::println) when ambiguousMethod has one overload taking a StringSink and one taking an IntSink?

options.text: It accepts the call and binds it to whichever overload the file declares first
options.says: Declaration order plays no part: the page says the compiler reports an error for this call.

options.text: It rejects the call with an error that a cast to one parameter type removes
options.says: The page's example reports the reference to ambiguousMethod as ambiguous and fixes it with an explicit cast.

options.text: It accepts the call and leaves the choice of overload to the running program
options.says: The page says method references are resolved at compile time, and this call is rejected there.
